title: Feature islands with parallel data copies
statement: Do not let CRM, prospecting, map, agenda or AI create independent copies of the same commercial entity.
risk: Creates parallel truths and inconsistent records across modules.

title: Copy an external architecture because it appears more mature
statement: External systems have different scale and constraints; transfer patterns only after problem and gap analysis.
risk: Imports irrelevant complexity, coupling and maintenance burden from reference systems.

title: Report unexecuted validation as success
statement: A test blocked by runtime/dependency/environment is BLOCKED/NOT RUN, never PASS.
risk: Creates false confidence and can ship unverified behavior.

title: Silent merge and resend after revision conflict
statement: Do not respond to an optimistic-concurrency conflict by merging snapshots and immediately writing the result without an explicit review boundary.
risk: The merge policy can silently choose one side of divergent business data, overwrite newer work, hide the conflict from the operator and turn optimistic concurrency into false safety.

title: Promote weak identifier matches directly into canonical truth
statement: Do not auto-create or auto-link canonical entities from a single weak or stale match such as normalized company name, partial identifier or an already-occupied candidate.
risk: A false positive can merge separate accounts, duplicate Companies, attach contacts to the wrong business and contaminate every downstream CRM, reporting and AI view that trusts the canonical model.

title: Parallel scoring, invented terminal actions and happy-path-only tests
statement: Do not duplicate scoring weights in another surface, invent a next action for terminal/no-action states, reuse cached guidance across materially different commercial context, or test only central functions while alternate UI paths bypass them.
risk: These shortcuts create contradictory priorities, stale guidance, false next steps and regressions that remain invisible despite unit tests on the canonical function.

title: Create a parallel project memory beside Builder Brain
statement: Do not create a second independent knowledge/context memory when the existing Builder Brain can be extended.
risk: Two memories disagree on current decisions, provenance and status, forcing agents to guess which history is authoritative.

title: Freeze volatile account facts inside global Skills
statement: Do not put current proposal status, latest conversation, negotiated account price, next action or other volatile customer facts inside global Skills/context files.
risk: Skill text becomes stale and competes with CRM/runtime truth, causing incorrect account advice.

title: Treat remembered deployment state as live runtime evidence
statement: Do not claim Railway health, deployed commit, environment configuration or live availability from chat/docs alone; verify current infrastructure.
risk: Historical runtime facts age quickly and can cause false success claims or unsafe operational decisions.

title: Use one commercial pitch for every account stage
statement: Do not use the same objective/script for a cold lead, gatekeeper, decision maker, active proposal, customer and post-sale account.
risk: The interaction ignores known relationship context, repeats work, weakens trust and can ask for expansion/referral before resolving the customer's actual state.

title: Promote code or remembered mappings into confirmed OG technical truth
statement: Do not present a support code, application, PSI, compatibility, product specification or performance claim as Confirmada OG solely because it appears in code or recovered chat history.
risk: Implementation history or informal notes can be incomplete/outdated and may produce a wrong physical application or unsupported commercial claim.

title: Evolve remote backend without versioning equivalent schema and function source in Git
statement: Do not treat a remote database migration or Edge Function deployment as complete if the repository cannot reproduce the resulting backend state.
risk: A future developer or agent can clone a green application repository yet be unable to rebuild, review or safely roll back the production backend, making recovery and security review dependent on undocumented remote state.
